note: Primary texts in their original languages, with a translation where one is free. Each link must pass tools/linkcheck.py.

items.title: Analects (論語), Confucius
items.note: Chinese text with James Legge’s English translation, line by line.

items.title: Dao De Jing (道德經), Laozi
items.note: Chinese with a parallel English translation.

items.title: Republic (Πολιτεία), Plato
items.note: Greek text with tap-a-word dictionary help; English by Paul Shorey.

items.title: Discours de la méthode (1637), Descartes
items.note: Where “I think, therefore I am” first appears, in French.

items.title: Nicomachean Ethics (Ἠθικὰ Νικομάχεια), Aristotle
items.note: Greek with W. D. Ross’s English translation.

items.title: Mencius (孟子)
items.note: The Confucian case that human nature is good, with English.

items.title: Histories (Ἱστορίαι), Herodotus
items.note: The first Greek history, with A. D. Godley’s translation.

items.title: Records of the Grand Historian (史記), Sima Qian
items.note: China’s founding work of history (c. 94 BCE), partly translated.

items.title: Muqaddimah (المقدمة), Ibn Khaldun
items.note: A 1377 theory of how states rise and fall, often called the first work of sociology.

items.title: Florentine Codex (General History of the Things of New Spain), Sahagún and Nahua scholars
items.note: A 1500s encyclopedia of Aztec life written by Indigenous authors, with pictures.

items.title: Il Principe (1532), Machiavelli
items.note: The original Italian.

items.title: Déclaration des droits de l’homme et du citoyen (1789)
items.note: Still part of France’s constitutional law today.

items.title: Grundgesetz (Basic Law of Germany, 1949)
items.note: Official German text and official English translation. Article 1: human dignity shall be inviolable.

items.title: Corpus Iuris Civilis, Justinian (529–534)
items.note: Roman law, the root of most legal systems in Europe and Latin America.

items.title: The Art of War (孫子兵法), Sunzi
items.note: Chinese with Lionel Giles’s English translation.

items.title: Vom Kriege (On War, 1832), Clausewitz
items.note: The 1832 German first edition.

items.title: Guanzi (管子)
items.note: Ancient Chinese writing on prices, grain reserves and state finance.

items.title: Das Kapital, Band 1 (1867), Marx
items.note: The original German.

items.title: Quran (القرآن)
items.note: Arabic text with translations in dozens of languages and recitation audio.

items.title: Tanakh (תנ״ך), the Hebrew Bible
items.note: Hebrew with English, plus centuries of commentary linked verse by verse.

items.title: Bhagavad Gita (भगवद्गीता)
items.note: Sanskrit with translations and commentaries, from IIT Kanpur.

items.title: Dhammapada
items.note: Early Buddhist verses in Pali with translations.

items.title: Iliad (Ἰλιάς), Homer
items.note: Greek with A. T. Murray’s English translation.

items.title: Divina Commedia, Dante
items.note: The poem that shaped the Italian language.

items.title: Don Quijote de la Mancha, Cervantes
items.note: Often called the first modern novel.

items.title: Book of Songs (詩經)
items.note: China’s oldest poetry (c. 1000–600 BCE), with English.

items.title: Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art (九章算術)
items.note: Han-dynasty problems, including solving systems of equations and negative numbers.

items.title: Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica (1687), Newton
items.note: A scan of the first edition, in Latin.

items.title: Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper (1905), Einstein
items.note: The special relativity paper as published in Annalen der Physik.

items.title: Mozi (墨子): the Mohist canons on optics
items.note: Includes one of the earliest descriptions of the pinhole camera (c. 400 BCE).

items.title: Huangdi Neijing (黃帝內經)
items.note: The founding text of Chinese medicine (c. 200s BCE). Historical, not a guide to treatment.

items.title: Shuowen Jiezi (說文解字), Xu Shen (100 CE)
items.note: The first Chinese dictionary to analyze characters by their parts.

items.title: Versuche über Pflanzen-Hybriden (1866), Mendel
items.note: The pea experiments that founded genetics.

items.title: De architectura, Vitruvius
items.note: Roman engineering and architecture, Latin with English, from LacusCurtius.

items.title: Tiangong Kaiwu (天工開物, 1637), Song Yingxing
items.note: An illustrated encyclopedia of Ming technology: bronze casting, paper, salt, weapons.
